glosses: To happen; to come to pass; to chance or light (upon).

examples.text: Sit still, my daughter, until thou know how the matter will fall.
[…]An the worst fall that ever fell, I hope I shall make shift to go without him.

[…] Polybius tells us, the beſt Government is that which conſiſts of three Forms, Regno, Optimatium, & Populi imperio. Which may be fairly Tranſlated, the Kings, Lords and Commons. […] the Romans fell upon this Model purely by chance, (which I take to have been Nature and common Reaſon) but the Spartans by Thought and Deſign.

1879, Herbert Spencer, Principles of Sociology Volume II – Part IV: Ceremonial Institutions
Primitive men […] do not make laws, they fall into customs.

glosses: To begin with haste, ardour, or vehemence; to rush or hurry.

examples.text: After arguing, they fell to blows.
They now no longer doubted, but fell to work heart and soul.

glosses: To be dropped or uttered carelessly.

examples.text: An unguarded expression fell from his lips.

glosses: To hang down (under the influence of gravity).

examples.text: An Empire-style dress has a high waistline – directly under the bust – from which the dress falls all the way to a hem as low as the floor.

glosses: To visit; to go to a place.

examples.text: We'll fall over to the club tonight.

glosses: The act of moving to a lower position under the effect of gravity.

examples.text: the fall of the snow
the fall of the water
the fall of the leaf

glosses: A reduction in quantity, pitch, etc.

examples.text: “I'm through with all pawn-games,” I laughed. “Come, let us have a game of lansquenet. Either I will take a farewell fall out of you or you will have your sevenfold revenge”.

glosses: The time of the year when the leaves typically fall from the trees; autumn; the season of the year between the autumnal equinox and the winter solstice.

examples.text: A friend has pointed out to me the following remark on this word: "In North America the season in which this [the fall of the leaf] takes place, derives its name from that circumstance, and instead of autumn is universally called the fall." [brackets in original]

glosses: A loss of greatness or status.

examples.text: the fall of Rome

glosses: That which falls or cascades.

examples.text: A fall of hair tumbled down one side of her body like a veil.
The heat of Daniel's gaze was nearly incendiary as he took in the fall of her hair spilling across her shoulders and down to her elbows.

glosses: The height of that which falls or cascades.
A crucial event or circumstance.
The action of a batsman being out.
A crucial event or circumstance.
A defect in the ice which causes stones thrown into an area to drift in a given direction.
A crucial event or circumstance.
An instance of a wrestler being pinned to the mat.
A hairpiece for women consisting of long strands of hair on a woven backing, intended primarily to cover hair loss.

examples.text: Female patients with localized hair loss on the top of scalp could select a fall or a demiwig to camouflage crown and anterior scalp loss.

glosses: Blame or punishment for a failure or misdeed.

examples.text: He set up his rival to take the fall.

glosses: The part of the rope of a tackle to which the power is applied in hoisting (usu. plural).

examples.text: Have the goodness to secure the falls of the mizzen halyards.
"[...] with one overhauled fall flying and an iron-bound block capering in the air."

glosses: An old Scots unit of measure equal to six ells.
A short, flexible piece of leather forming part of a bullwhip, placed between the thong and the cracker.

examples.text: Brooks fitted a new fall to his whip.

glosses: The lid, on a piano, that covers the keyboard.
The cry given when a whale is sighted, or harpooned.
The chasing of a hunted whale.
